reports.content: Personality assessment: Tom is diligent in maintaining detailed journal entries after each trading session, carefully analyzing his decisions and outcomes. Despite having a logical understanding of market fluctuations, he sometimes experiences frustration when a trade results in a loss. Tom sets a goal of achieving at least a 5% monthly return by continuously refining his trading strategies and staying disciplined. He shows a preference for technical analysis tools over fundamental analysis to make informed decisions. Tom methodically approaches the study of new trading strategies, dedicating a week to evaluate their effectiveness before any implementation. Every Sunday, he reviews his trades, using the insights gained to adjust his plans for the upcoming week.

messages.content: I've been looking over my journal, and I noticed some patterns with how I trade AAPL.
What sort of patterns are standing out to you?
Well, I consistently record after each session, and it seems like I'm catching the same impulsive entries. I write down everything, like what I was feeling and what led me to the decision.
That sounds thorough. How do those entries help you evaluate your decisions?
They really highlight the emotional triggers. For example, last Thursday I got in on TSLA because I felt like I was missing out, even though I had a rule against chasing.
How often do you review your previous entries?
I do it weekly. It's like a ritual now, going over each detail and seeing what I can improve.
And what do you think is the benefit of maintaining that routine?
It keeps me accountable. I can't ignore the mistakes or the successes; everything's there in black and white.
Sounds like a solid approach. How would you say this impacts your trading overall?
It's made a huge difference in my self-awareness. I catch myself making fewer mistakes, like those impulsive trades.
